key_headlines.summary: Vice Minister Huh Jang showcased South Korea's economic performance to global investors in Paris, highlighting the nation's top OECD growth rate, strong exports exceeding $390 billion (up 40% YoY), and consecutive current account surplus.

key_headlines.title: Full Currency Crisis Looms: Won Falls to Weakest Level Since 2009 Despite 36-Month Current Account Surplus
key_headlines.summary: Despite recording 36 consecutive months of current account surplus totaling $102.67 billion in Jan-Apr, the Korean won has weakened to its lowest level since the 2008-09 financial crisis, driven by foreign investor stock outflows and rising global oil prices.

key_headlines.title: South Korea Stock Markets Plunge on Global Uncertainty, KOSPI Falls 5.54%
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI dropped 478.82 points (5.54%) to 8,160.59 and KOSDAQ fell 4.50%, marking a 'Black Friday' with the won-dollar rate surging past 1,540 won for the first time since the global financial crisis amid Middle East tensions and foreign investor selloffs.

key_headlines.title: Government Fast-Tracks Jangseong Advanced Data Center Construction in Jeollanam-do for AI Infrastructure
key_headlines.summary: The government is expediting a 400 billion won advanced data center project in Jangseong, Jeollanam-do by exempting it from local fiscal investment reviews, targeting completion by 2027 and operations launch by 2028 to strengthen regional AI infrastructure.

key_headlines.title: Labor Minister Emphasizes AI Excess Profit Redistribution as Reinvestment, Not Communism
key_headlines.summary: Labor Minister Kim Young-hoon stated that large corporations' AI excess profits should be redistributed to suppliers through contract price adjustments as part of co-prosperity measures, framing it as reinvestment rather than ideological redistribution.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea is experiencing strong macroeconomic momentum with Q1 GDP growth of 1.7% leading OECD countries and exports surging 40% year-over-year to $390 billion during Jan-May. However, this strength is being undermined by currency weakness, with the won falling to 2009 financial crisis lows despite 36 consecutive months of current account surplus ($102.67 billion in Jan-Apr). Vice Minister Huh Jang presented Korea's investment appeal at a Paris OECD roadshow, emphasizing capital market reforms and foreign investment inflows of $18.7 billion in government bonds. The government is also accelerating infrastructure investments, including a 400 billion won AI-focused data center in Jeollanam-do, though global uncertainties continue to pressure domestic financial markets.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's 1.7% Q1 GDP growth leads OECD member states, with the OECD raising its 2026 growth forecast to 2.6% from 1.7% and lowering the general government debt ratio to GDP projection to 48.2% from 52.0%. Strong export performance (up over 40% YoY) and record current account surpluses of $102.67 billion in Jan-Apr demonstrate robust external economic conditions. However, authorities are expressing caution about financial volatility and inflation, with the Bank of Korea expected to raise the base rate in July due to rising oil prices and favorable economic conditions. Government officials emphasize the importance of fiscal-growth virtuous cycle while remaining vigilant against price pressures and currency volatility.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korea's stock markets experienced severe turbulence on June 5, with KOSPI plummeting 5.54% to 8,160.59 and KOSDAQ falling 4.50% to 1,002.44 amid global uncertainty and Middle East tensions. The won-dollar exchange rate surged past 1,540 for the first time since 2009, reaching 1,539.10 won, driven by persistent foreign investor selling over 20 consecutive trading days. Program trading circuit breakers were triggered due to the sharp KOSPI decline, while analysts suggest the index could recover to 11,800 by year-end if corporate earnings remain strong despite volatility. Oil price increases and geopolitical risks are intensifying market swings, though underlying economic fundamentals remain supportive of equities.
sections.Industry & Technology: SK Siltroon's tier-one supplier Dajin Machinery, a semiconductor wafer equipment and EV battery equipment manufacturer, is being shopped for acquisition. Prediction, an EV operation optimization AI platform startup, has launched its 'EView' beta service with 10 vehicle subscription contracts including mid-sized logistics firm Ilyang Logistics. China's BYD, the world's leading EV manufacturer, has announced entry into the humanoid robot development sector. Japan's government unveiled plans to rebuild up to 5 nuclear power plants by the 2040s with maximum capacity of 5.5 million kW, representing about 20% of Japan's current nuclear fleet.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's real estate market faces critical challenges with rapid monthly rent increases and plummeting jeonse (deposit rental) listings, prompting newly elected Mayor Oh Se-hun to prioritize housing policy reform. Officetels registered a 9.1% increase in lease transactions in Jan-Apr 2026 as demand shifted from apartments due to limited jeonse inventory, which dropped 28.7% compared to last year. Price-capped apartments under the price ceiling system achieved 2.5 times higher subscription competition rates than general units due to affordability concerns amid skyrocketing market prices. Mayor Oh's administration plans to accelerate private redevelopment and reconstruction projects, targeting 310,000 housing unit starts by 2031 to stabilize prices.
sections.International Economy: Fed officials are increasingly hawkish, with even Trump-aligned personnel suggesting potential interest rate hikes despite earlier expectations of economic stimulus under the new administration. CME FedWatch data shows markets now price in a 41.1% probability of rate hikes in December 2026, up sharply from 9.1% a month earlier, reflecting significantly changed market expectations. SpaceX launched its IPO roadshow with Goldman Sachs projecting 100-fold growth in AI business revenue by 2030, underscoring AI's centrality to future valuations. U.S. stock markets declined amid Middle East tensions and rising oil prices, while Trump signaled willingness to reach trade agreements with India, though both nations maintain significant tariff disputes.
sections.AI & Economy: South Korea's Labor Minister Kim Young-hoon emphasized that large corporations' AI excess profits should be redistributed through supplier contract price adjustments as part of co-prosperity measures, framing this as reinvestment rather than communist-style redistribution. SpaceX's IPO roadshow highlighted projections that AI business revenue could grow 100-fold by 2030, with Goldman Sachs suggesting AI growth is critical to realizing the company's $1.77 trillion valuation. Amazon announced 18 trillion won investment in Europe for warehouse automation using conversational AI robots, while emphasizing that automation drives job creation rather than displacement—the company hired hundreds of thousands of additional workers post-robotization. Government discussions focus on sharing AI-driven excess profits across the value chain to ensure equitable benefit distribution.
sections.Others: The U.S. Trump administration confirmed a major milestone in small modular reactor (SMR) development, with the first Antares SMR achieving critical mass success as a key step toward commercialization. South Korea and Serbia concluded a landmark CEPA (Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement), marking the Balkans' first such economic alliance with Korea, with Serbia serving as Korea's 97th export destination and 87th import source. TerraPower, an advanced SMR company backed by SK, achieved a significant construction feat in the U.S. desert, completing a 35-meter facility in just three months, advancing Trump's nuclear renaissance agenda. President Trump privately indicated he would not escalate into full-scale warfare with Iran unless U.S. military casualties occur, representing a potential variable in ongoing U.S.-Iran peace negotiations.
